problem: Prior VLN methods (including agricultural AgriVLN) assume the given instruction is correct, but real users often say instructions with mistakes; the only prior study (R2RIE-CE) relies on fully manual annotation and a detector that uses images from all time steps, which an agent cannot access at the start.
motivation: Humans doubt an instruction when the scene does not match it, but VLN agents lack this awareness. Agricultural robots need robustness to speaking mistakes from workers, so a benchmark and a mechanism for detecting and correcting instruction mistakes are needed.
key_idea: Prompt a VLM with two principles (conservative verification, minimal intervention) to check the instruction/current subtask against the current front camera image, then localize and minimally correct the mistaken span, plugged into AgriVLN.
insight: Inserting a single-word mistake causes large drops for all agents (AgriVLN SR 0.23 to 0.10 avg), so agents implicitly trust instructions; verb mistakes hurt most (NE 4.86). In the ablation, IMAC alone gives SR 0.13 versus STL alone 0.10, so IMAC is the main contributor, and the two are complementary (0.14 SR). The failure case shows over-aggressive correction can inject noise when the target is outside the current view.
method: A2A-MI benchmark: keeps A2A images and inserts three mistake classes (descriptive adjective, concrete noun, behavioral verb) by replacing a same-length contiguous span, giving 4,680 episodes (3x1,560).
Semi-automatic annotator: an LLM zero-shot generates 3 candidate revisions per class, and a human specialist picks the most reasonable one.

IMAC module: a zero-shot VLM takes the instruction and image and outputs the mistaken span, the corrected instruction and a decision summary. The system prompt sets Conservative Verification and Minimal Intervention.

Integration into AgriVLN: IMAC is called once at start with W and I_0 before the STL decomposition, and again at each step on the current subtask description D_i* and I_t, updating D, SC, EC if a mistake is found.
AR metric: Instruction Mistake Valid Awareness Rate, equal to 1 if any predicted mistaken span across the episode equals the labeled span.

setting.backbone: DeepSeek-R1-32B (Q4_K_M, LLM for STL) + Qwen2.5-VL-32B (Q4_K_M, VLM for decision-maker and IMAC), frozen, zero-shot prompting
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD / LEFT ROTATE / RIGHT ROTATE / STOP
setting.simulator: none; real-world recorded A2A video/image episodes
setting.privileged: none (deviation from ground-truth action sequence is used as episode termination criterion, following A2A)

numbers.extra: average over adj/noun/verb mistake classes; SR uses 2 m threshold; A2A-MI is evaluation-only
numbers.evidence: Table comparison (#6 IMAC-AgriVLN avg SR 0.14, NE 4.79) and Table AR (#8 avg 0.27)

numbers.method: IMAC-AgriVLN (no mistakes inserted, original A2A instructions)

numbers.extra: ablation, average across three mistake classes

numbers_note: Values are on the paper's own A2A-MI benchmark (not a canonical benchmark); SR is printed as fractions (0.14), not percent. Per-class values: IMAC-AgriVLN SR adj 0.14 / noun 0.15 / verb 0.13; NE 4.77 / 4.72 / 4.87; AR 0.09 / 0.57 / 0.15.
results: On A2A-MI all agents drop sharply (AgriVLN SR 0.23 to avg 0.10). IMAC-AgriVLN raises avg SR from 0.10 to 0.14 and lowers NE from 4.81 to 4.79 m, with AR 0.27, but DILLM-VLN has the lowest NE (4.31 avg) and humans reach SR 0.77, so a big gap remains.
limitations: Correction is imperfect (AR 0.27, only 0.09 on adjectives); over-aggressive correction can turn correct words into errors when the target is out of view
No metric for correction quality; AR only checks the span, not the replacement
NE gain is marginal (4.81 to 4.79) and DILLM-VLN has better NE; mistakes are single-span synthetic insertions, evaluated only in one benchmark
